remarks_1999: Not recorded Whitney Archive, Downtown Gallery Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks. Dated 1943 on basis of Stieglitz–O'Keeffe correspondence. O'Keeffe wrote: "I first met Beauford Delaney when he was posing for Mary Callery. I found that he was a painter and posed for others because he had no heat in his studio and needed to keep warm. He seemed a very special sort of person so I began drawing him too" (*Some Memories of Drawings* [1988], unpaginated). See cat. nos. 1042–45. (Source: Lynes, 1999)

titles.notes: Source of title: relationship of image to cat. nos. 1042, 1045.
titles.title: Untitled (Beauford Delaney)

credit_line: Gift of The Georgia O'Keeffe Foundation
description: Depicts Beauford Delaney, an American modernist painter. In this composition his head is situated on the upper half of the sheet of paper. He has a serious expression on his face, and his eyes look slightly off to the viewer's left.
